title: I'd Rather Be Reading: The Delights and Dilemmas of the Reading Life
author: Anne Bogel
target_audience: Anyone who loves stories and reading culture
Readers seeking literary inspiration and connection
core_themes: The profound joy and solace of reading
How reading shapes identity and life experiences
The unique dilemmas faced by devoted readers (e.g., overflowing shelves, TBR guilt)
The communal and personal aspects of reading life
primary_purpose: To celebrate the joys and acknowledge the tribulations of a life shaped by reading, offering reflections, anecdotes, and gentle humor for those who see books as a vital part of who they are.

structure_format.organization: A collection of short essays and musings, each focused on different facets of the reading life
features: Occasional book recommendations and literary references

key_concepts_lessons: Books not only entertain, but form a lens through which readers understand themselves and the world.
The act of choosing, shelving, lending, and discussing books is as meaningful as reading itself.
Readers often experience dilemmas unique to their passion, such as feeling overwhelmed by unread books or remembering formative library visits.
Sharing the reading experience deepens connection—to others and one’s own reading journey.
There is no right or wrong way to be a reader; the quirks and customs are part of the delight.
notable_features: Highly relatable and specific to reading culture
Humor and warmth in exploring the reader’s identity
Ideal as a gift for book lovers
Frequent references to other books and authors
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2018, the book taps into a renewed cultural celebration of reading—through social media book clubs, bookish communities, and a wider recognition of reading as meaningful self-care.
reception_impact: Embraced by the online reading community (especially fans of Bogel’s ‘Modern Mrs Darcy’ blog and podcast)
Praised for authenticity, relatability, and gentle humor
Frequently recommended as a gift for bibliophiles
Noted for capturing the true spirit and peculiarities of the reading life
comparable_titles: The Library Book by Susan Orlean
Ex Libris: Confessions of a Common Reader by Anne Fadiman
So Many Books, So Little Time by Sara Nelson
